question.text: Under the AIF Regulations, winding up of a scheme can be triggered when:

answer.text: The tenure (or extended tenure) of the scheme expires without the required investor consent, or SEBI directs winding up in the investors' interests

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook (pp.68 and 220) sets out Regulation 29 winding-up grounds: expiry of the tenure or extended tenure (where consent for further extension is not obtained), the trustees forming an opinion that winding up is in investors' interests, a resolution passed by at least 75% of investors (by value), or SEBI directing the scheme to be wound up in the investors' interests. The Trap: Completing all investments, achieving a target return, or having unanimous investor consent are not, by themselves, the regulatory triggers. SEBI does not "revoke registration" as the trigger — the registration certificate is surrendered after the scheme is wound up. Note: Source references: NISM Series XIX-A workbook pp.68 and 220 (Regulation 29 winding-up triggers — tenure expiry without consent, trustee opinion, 75% investor resolution, SEBI direction).
